note: Portfolio of Pacific Pro Group project models. Add a project: put its house config next to this file, add an entry here, run python3 portfolio_site.py.

projects.title: Magnolia house, basement ADU and garage
projects.card: Remodel of a one-story house over a daylight basement, with a new 865 SF basement ADU and a detached one-car garage.
projects.firstLine: The finished house, the ADU below it, and the garage. Choose Explore to turn the model or go to a room.
projects.dek: Explore the Magnolia project layer by layer: the finished house, the roof, the main level, the basement ADU and the foundation.
projects.sourceNote: Traced from the permit sets. Unprinted dimensions are scaled by eye from the sheets.

projects.title: One-story house with shop and garage
projects.card: A one-story layout, 6,720 SF total as printed: primary suite, two bedrooms, open kitchen, living and dining with a 14 foot ceiling, a den, and a large attached garage with a shop.
projects.dek: Explore this one-story layout layer by layer: the finished house, the roof, the floor plan with every room, and the slab.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from a one-page layout plan. Walls, openings, room names, areas and ceiling heights come from the plan. The roof, window sills and heads, and door heights are not drawn on the plan and are shown as labeled assumptions.
assumptions: Roof: not drawn on the layout. Assumed hipped roofs at 4:12 with 18 inch overhangs over every wing, meeting in hips and valleys.

Garage and shop walls are assumed at 16 feet; the layout prints no garage ceiling height. The whole garage and shop wing shares one roof with one ridge height: past the 16 foot wide north bay's ridge line the slope eases to a 1/2:12 deck, so nothing steps down mid garage.
The house roof sits on its 9 foot walls and rises into the taller garage wall, so no pocket is left where they meet, and stays clear of the rear garage door by the walk-in closet.
The covered patio roof runs unbroken along the whole north face at the 9 foot eave. The living and dining room roof is raised behind it over the 14 foot ceiling, with short clerestory walls.
The layout prints 9 foot ceilings for the Primary Bedroom, Kitchen and Den, so those walls stay at 9 feet.
Dining and sink bay sizes are scaled from the layout; bay sills and the bay roof height are assumed.
Exterior door leaves are shown at an assumed 6 foot 8 inch height; the Primary Bedroom corner doors are shown as glazed French doors.

projects.title: Two-story house with attached garage
projects.card: A two-story house from an approved permit set, 3,063 SF conditioned: open dining, kitchen and living under a 10 foot ceiling, a dining room open to the floor above, a primary suite, two bedrooms, two offices and a 12 foot garage.
projects.dek: Explore this two-story house layer by layer: the finished house, the roof, the upper floor, the main floor with every room, and the slab.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from the approved permit set: both floor plans, the roof plan, four elevations, the building section and the window and door schedules. Walls, openings, room names, areas, ceiling heights, roof pitches and the overall height come from those sheets. Anything the sheets do not print is listed below as an assumption.

roof: From the roof plan and elevations: a 5:12 main gable, a 10:12 cross gable with gable ends on both sides, a 9 5/8:12 gable over the garage, an 11:12 dormer gable and a 5:12 porch roof on three posts. Overhangs are 18 inches and the roofing is asphalt shingle. The highest point is 32'-2" above average grade, as printed.
garage: The garage is 460 SF with a 12 foot ceiling. Its slab sits three risers below the main floor, with a 16 by 7 foot overhead door and a side door.
header: Window and door sizes come from the schedules and sit in the wall gaps drawn on the plans. Heads are set at 6'-8" to line up with the doors, as the elevations show; sills follow from each scheduled window height.
partition: Room names, areas and ceiling heights are the ones printed on the plans: 10 feet on the main floor, 9 feet upstairs and 12 feet in the garage. The dining room is open to the upper floor. Select a room to fly in.
foundation: A slab on grade under the main floor, and the garage slab three risers lower.

assumptions: Window heads at 6'-8" are scaled from the elevations, where they line up with the door heads. Sills are the head minus the scheduled window height.
Upper floor framing is drawn 1'-6" deep, scaled from the elevation level lines.
The main floor sits 1'-11" above the garage slab (three printed risers at 7 3/4 inches). The ground is drawn flat at the garage slab.
Dormer eave and porch roof heights are scaled from the south and west elevations.
The stair is drawn as a straight run of 18 risers at the printed 7 3/4 inch rise. The turn at its foot is simplified.
Furniture and fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Interior doors are shown as open frames.

The plan examiner's markups on the approved set are applied: the laundry wall moved 1'-6" west, the Office 01 door moved to the hall side, an upstairs door replaced by a 40 inch archway into the primary bedroom, a floor to ceiling window on the main floor north wall, and the larger side patio.
The markups print only 1'-6", 18' and 40 inches. The moved office door, the archway, the new window and the patio's diagonal edge are scaled from the hand sketch and may be off by several inches.
The floor to ceiling window runs from the floor to 9'-6". Its head height is not printed.

Room areas are the printed ones, except the upstairs laundry. Its area was printed as 75.84 SF before the markup moved its wall, so the label shows the redlined area as modeled, about 96 SF. The open living room and the two halls have no drawn boundaries, so their outlines are approximate.
Siding, stone veneer, deck and porch railings and trim colors are not modeled.

projects.title: One-story house with a new second story
projects.card: A second-story addition from a plan set: a full new upper floor over an existing one-story house, with a primary suite, two bedrooms, two baths and a storage room under one 6:12 gable roof. The first floor keeps its rooms and gains a mudroom and a new stair.
projects.dek: Explore the addition layer by layer: the finished house, the roof, the new second floor, the existing first floor with its new mudroom and stair, and the floor platform.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from the plan set: the proposed first and second floor plans, the roof plan and four proposed elevations. Walls, openings, room names, the printed areas, floor and plate heights, the roof pitch and the overhangs come from those sheets. Anything the sheets do not print is listed below as an assumption.

roof: From the roof plan and elevations: one 6:12 gable over the whole house, with its gable ends on the deck side and the shed side, 18 inch overhangs and asphalt shingles. The new wall plate is printed at 17'-0" above the first floor, so the ridge sits about 23'-5" above it.
header: New windows and doors use the sizes printed beside them on the plans, such as 72 by 60 inch bedroom windows and 30 by 80 inch doors. Existing first floor openings are only marked existing, so their widths are the wall gaps on the plan and their heights are scaled from the elevations.
partition: Second floor rooms show their printed areas, with 9 foot walls between the printed 8'-0" second floor and the 17'-0" plate. The existing first floor rooms have no printed areas, so they show names only. Select a room to fly in.

assumptions: The overall size, 25'-8" by 41'-2", is printed with a note to verify it in the field. Walls are traced from the plan linework at 1/4 inch = 1 foot.
The first floor sits 2 feet above the ground, scaled from the deck skirt and stair on the deck-side elevation. The site slope is not modeled; the ground is drawn flat.

First floor walls run the printed 8'-0" from the first floor to the second floor. The first floor ceiling height and the floor framing depth are not printed; the framing is drawn about 11 inches deep.

Window heads are scaled from the elevations: about 7'-0" on the first floor and 8'-0" above the second floor. Sills follow from the printed window heights. Existing first floor windows are drawn 4 feet tall, scaled.
The second floor stair window has no printed size. It is drawn 3 by 5 feet, scaled from the elevation.
Existing first floor openings are marked existing without sizes. Their widths are the wall gaps on the plan, and door heads are 6'-8".
The ridge height is not printed. It follows from the printed 17'-0" plate and the 6:12 pitch.
The stair is drawn as two straight flights with a landing, 15 risers in all. The riser count is not printed; the plans note a 7 inch maximum riser.
The existing shed and its roof stay as they are. Their heights are scaled from the elevations.
Existing first floor rooms have no printed areas, so their labels show names only.
Furniture and fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Interior doors are shown as open frames.
Siding, trim, deck railings and exterior lights are not modeled.

projects.title: Hillside post-and-beam house with a lower-level ADU
projects.card: Preliminary design for a new custom post-and-beam home on a sloping lot: a main floor with a planted roof, a primary suite upstairs and a daylight lower-level ADU with two bedrooms that opens to the back patio.
projects.dek: Explore the preliminary design layer by layer: the house on its slope, the entry side, the flat and planted roofs, the upper floor, the main floor and the lower-level ADU.
projects.sourceNote: Preliminary design, modeled from the design drawings: the main, upper and lower level plans at 1/8 inch = 1 foot, four elevations and the 3D plan views. Walls, wall openings, room names, the level areas, the floor to floor heights and the roof outline come from those sheets. The design may still change. Anything the sheets do not print is listed below as an assumption.

roof: From the elevations and the 3D views: two flat, low roofs with deep overhangs, one over the main floor and one over the upper floor. The main roof outline is drawn on the upper level plan, where it is labeled green roof. The back elevation prints three 10'-6" steps, so the main roof sits 10'-6" above the main floor and the upper roof 10'-6" above the upper floor.
header: Window and door widths are the gaps in the exterior walls on the plans, mostly 4'-11" bays between the posts of the 5'-6" building grid. The plans print no window schedule, so sills and heads are scaled from the elevations by window type: tall glass to the back, high transom windows on the street sides.
partition: The plans print the area of each level but no room areas, so rooms show their names only. Select a room to fly in.

assumptions: This is a preliminary design. The drawings say the design may change.
Walls are traced from the plan drawings at 1/8 inch = 1 foot, checked against the printed 5'-6" building grid. No overall dimensions are printed.
Floor to floor heights are the printed 10'-6" steps on the back elevation. Walls stop 1'-0" below the next level for the roof and floor edge; that depth is scaled from the elevations.
Window and door heights are scaled from the elevations by window type. There is no window or door schedule.

The main roof outline is the line drawn on the upper level plan. The upper roof overhang, about 2'-0", is scaled from the elevations. Both roofs are drawn flat; their slope for drainage is not printed.
The green roof is drawn over the whole main roof outside the upper floor, as the upper level plan labels it. Planting and parapet details are not shown.

The ground is drawn as simple planes scaled from the side elevations: level with the lower floor behind the house, rising to the main floor on the street side, and stepping down beside the walk stair to the lower level entry. The lot shape, the full 16 foot fall across the lot and any retaining walls are not modeled.
The stairs are drawn as straight flights of 17 risers, scaled from the plans. The riser count is not printed.
The walk steps between the lower entry and the main level walk are the nine treads drawn on the plans; their rise is assumed even.
Two rooms with no printed name are labeled Bath (unlabeled) from their plumbing fixtures.

The two deck columns are the outlined 2'-0" x 6" rectangles on the deck edges of the main level plan. The deck guard follows the back and side elevations: horizontal metal bars with a dark top rail, about 3'-0" above the deck (scaled), with a wood rim band under the deck edge.
The north walk stair to the lower level entry is drawn as on the plans. No retaining wall is drawn on the plans, so none is modeled.

Furniture and fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Their heights are assumed. Interior doors are shown as open gaps, except the upper laundry bi-fold doors and the bonus room closet doors, drawn open as the plan shows them.
Beam ends under the overhangs are the dashed beam lines on the plans where they run past the walls. Their 1'-0" depth is scaled from the back elevation.
Siding, cedar trim and soffits, posts and beams inside the glass walls, and window mullions are not modeled. The entry door is shown in warm wood, as on the front elevation.

projects.title: Attached house with a new second story
projects.card: A second-story addition from a plan set: a full new upper floor over one side of a one-story duplex, with a primary bedroom, two walk-in closets, a large bath, a laundry closet and a third bedroom under a new 6:12 gable. The other unit keeps its one-story roof.
facts: New upper floor over the whole unit
projects.dek: Explore the addition layer by layer: the finished house beside its neighbor unit, the entry side, the new roof, the new upper floor, the main floor with its new stair and the floor platform.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from the plan set: the proposed main and upper floor plans, the roof plan and the existing and proposed elevations at 1/4 inch = 1 foot. Walls, openings, window sizes, room names, the floor, plate and ridge heights, the roof pitch and the overhangs come from those sheets. Anything the sheets do not print is listed below as an assumption.

roof: From the roof plan and elevations: a new 6:12 gable over the whole addition side with its ridge running front to back, 2'-0" eaves and flared rakes that widen to about 2'-0" at the ridge. A small gable covers the upstairs closet bump on the entry side and runs into the main roof. The other unit keeps its existing gable, and the porch roof along the entry side stays in the plane of the existing roof. The new ridge is printed 24'-0 5/8" above the main floor.
header: New windows use the sizes printed beside them, such as NEW 6046 (6'-0" wide, 4'-6" tall) and NEW 5070 for the new sliding door. Heads are the printed 7'-4 1/4" on the main floor and 6'-11 3/8" on the upper floor, so each sill follows from the printed height. Existing openings are marked existing only; their heights are scaled from the elevations.
partition: The plans print room names but no room areas, so rooms show their names only. The upper floor sits 9'-6 5/8" above the main floor with a 9'-1 1/8" plate. The other unit is outside the work and is shown as a closed shell. Select a room to fly in.

assumptions: The house is one side of a one-story duplex. Only this side is in the work, so the other unit is drawn as a closed shell from the plan outline and the elevations, with no interior.
Walls are traced from the plan drawings at 1/4 inch = 1 foot. Few overall dimensions are printed; the traced main floor matches the printed 650 SF existing first floor within 1 percent.
The other unit's walls are drawn 5 1/2 inches thick inside its plan outline, the same as this side. Its windows and doors are placed from the elevations.
Existing window heads are the printed 7'-4 1/4". The existing sills, about 2'-4", and the high kitchen windows over the counter, about 4'-4" to 6'-2", are scaled from the elevations.
The two entry doors are shown 6'-8" tall. Their tops are hidden behind the porch roof edge on the elevations.

The roof planes are set to meet the printed ridge at the printed +/-6:12 pitch, so the roof sits about 4 inches above the printed plate at the wall line (the rafter heel). The same rule sets the existing roof from its printed ridge.
The flared rakes are scaled from the roof plan: about 4 inches at the eave, widening to 2'-0" at the ridge.
The porch roof along the entry side follows the existing roof plane out to the eave line drawn 2'-0" past the bumps. Porch posts are not drawn on the plans and are not modeled.

The stair has the printed 15 risers, about 7 5/8 inches each. The landing after nine risers matches the landing line printed on the south elevation; the two steps on the lower landing are read from the plan lines.
The south stair window, NEW 4046, sits 2'-0" above the landing, as printed on the south elevation.
The 2'-0" deep bump on the south wall at the party line is drawn on the plans with no label. It is shown as a closed box up to the eave.
The concrete porch and the heat pump pad are scaled from the main floor plan. The ground is flat at the printed 9 inch floor height.
Kitchen, bath and closet fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Their heights are assumed. Interior doors are shown as open gaps.
Siding, the stone wainscot at the kitchen bumps, the trim bands at the floor line, window grids and the solar tubes are not modeled.

projects.title: Daylight basement house with an attached garage
projects.card: A permit set for an existing house, drawn as built: a one-story main floor with an attached garage over a finished daylight basement that opens to a deck on the low side of the lot, plus a basement bath remodel with a new tub and shower.
projects.kicker: North King County, as-built permit and bath remodel
projects.dek: Explore the house layer by layer: the house on its slope, the street side, the roof, the main floor, the finished basement and the basement slab.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from the plan set: the existing basement and main floor plans and the proposed basement plan at 1/4 inch = 1 foot. Walls, openings, room names, the stair, the decks and the bath remodel come from those sheets. The set has no elevations, roof plan, window schedule or ceiling heights, so every height and the roof are assumptions, listed below.

roof: The plan set has no roof plan and no elevations, so the roof is an assumption: a hipped roof at 4:12 with 18 inch overhangs over the traced walls of the house and the garage, all at one plate height. The chimney for the two fireplaces is not drawn and is not modeled.
header: Window and door widths are traced from the plans, where every opening is marked existing (EXST'G), some also EGRESS. The set has no window schedule, so every window is shown with an assumed 3'-0" sill and 6'-10" head, doors 6'-8" tall and the garage door 7'-0" tall.
partition: The plans print room names but no room areas, so rooms show their names only. Both levels are traced at 1/4 inch = 1 foot; the stair has the 14 risers drawn. Select a room to fly in.

assumptions: Walls are traced from the existing basement and main floor plans at 1/4 inch = 1 foot and checked against the printed dimensions. The traced main floor is about 1,940 SF to the outside faces against the printed 1,920 SF, and the two decks trace to about 800 SF, as printed.

No ceiling or floor heights are printed. The stair has 14 risers drawn, so the main floor is set 8'-9" above the basement floor (7 1/2 inch risers). Ceilings are assumed 7'-9" in the basement and 8'-0" on the main floor.
The roof is not drawn: a 4:12 hipped roof with 18 inch overhangs is assumed over the traced walls, with the house and the garage at one plate height. The chimney is not drawn and is not modeled.
Window sizes are not printed. Widths are traced from the plans; every window is shown with a 3'-0" sill and a 6'-10" head, doors 6'-8" tall and the 16'-3" garage door 7'-0" tall.

The ground is not drawn. It is set level with the basement floor along the deck side and the shop end, where the basement has windows, a sliding door and an outside door, and 9 inches under the main floor on the street side, where the garage and the entry porch are. It slopes between the two along the kitchen end and the street side of the shop.
The garage slab is assumed 6 inches below the main floor. The porch and its step are scaled from the plan with assumed heights; the walk is drawn only as far as the sheet shows it.

The upper deck is drawn 5'-0" deep at the main floor with a guard. Its posts are not drawn; posts are shown at the corners and about every 8 feet down to the lower deck. The lower deck follows the drawn outline at the basement floor.
Both fireplaces are shown as solid masonry blocks at their drawn size.
The basement bath is shown as remodeled on the proposed plan: vanity, toilet and a combination tub and shower between two new 2x6 walls.
The plans label two main floor rooms Bedroom and two Bath; they are numbered here so the room picker can tell them apart.

Kitchen, laundry and bath fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Their heights are assumed. Interior door leaves are shown open where the plans draw them: swing doors at a right angle, pocket doors part way into the wall and the bypass closet doors overlapped. Closet shelving, siding and trim are not modeled.

projects.title: One-story house with a bedroom addition and remodel
projects.card: An approved permit set for a one-story house: a new bedroom and hall filled in between the two west wings under a low hip roof, with the primary suite, both baths, the walk-in closet and the kitchen remodeled and the kitchen opened to the family room.
projects.dek: Explore the house layer by layer: the finished house, the entry side, the roof, the floor plan, the rooms and the floor.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from the approved plan set: the proposed floor plan, roof plan, elevations and section at 1/4 inch = 1 foot. Walls, openings, room names, window sizes, the roof shape and pitches and the printed plate, header and ridge heights come from those sheets. Anything the sheets do not show is an assumption, listed below.

roof: The roof follows the proposed roof plan: 6:12 gables over the primary bedroom wing, the family room wing, the second bedroom and the main block, and a hip at 4 5/32:12 over the new bedroom that meets the 6:12 slopes in hips and valleys. The elevations print the ridge 18'-8 1/4" above the floor. Overhangs are scaled from the roof plan: 18 inches at the eaves, 2 feet at the addition and 3 inches at the rakes.
header: Window and door widths are traced from the floor plan and their heights read off the elevations, which print a 6'-11 3/8" window header. New windows carry their tags (5040, 3620, 5036: width and height in feet and inches); the rest are marked existing (EXST'G).
partition: The plan prints room names but no room areas except the 265 SF addition, so rooms show their names only. Select a room to fly in.

assumptions: Walls are traced from the proposed floor plan at 1/4 inch = 1 foot and checked against the printed dimensions. The traced house is about 1,934 SF to the outside faces against the printed 1,895 SF main floor; the addition traces to 265.6 SF against the printed 265 SF.
Heights come from the proposed elevations: top plate 8'-1 1/8", window header 6'-11 3/8" and ridge 18'-8 1/4" above the floor. Ceilings are assumed 8'-0" and interior doors 6'-8".

The roof follows the proposed roof plan with the printed 6:12 and 4 5/32:12 pitches. Where the roof plan and the ridge height leave the eave height open, the roof planes are set to meet the printed ridge; the roof covering is shown as plain courses.

The ground is set from the elevations: about 2'-0" below the floor on the north and west sides, falling to about 2'-5" at the northeast corner and rising to about 1'-4" below the floor at the southeast corner. The crawl space under the floor is not shown.
The entry stoop, its steps down along the wall and its railing are scaled from the floor plan and the east and north elevations; the number of steps is assumed.
Window widths are traced from the plan; window heights are read off the elevations. The 3'-4" entry door is shown at the window header height.
The plans label two rooms Bath and three Bdrm; they are numbered here so the room picker can tell them apart.

Kitchen, bath, laundry and bedroom fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Their heights are assumed. Interior doors are shown as open gaps. Closet shelving, siding, the stone wainscot and trim are not modeled.

projects.title: Split-level duplex conversion
projects.card: A split-level duplex drawn for a conversion study: a basement and a first floor unit stacked in a two-story block, with a one-story ground floor wing half a level between them. The owner's sketch joins the ground and first floors by opening the stair between them.
facts: Three levels, half a level apart
projects.dek: Explore the house layer by layer: the finished house, the street side, the roofs, the first floor, the ground floor and the basement.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from the architect's existing and demolition floor plans for all three levels at 3/16 inch = 1 foot, the site plan and the owner's marked-up conversion sketches. Walls, openings, stairs, room names and the printed room sizes come from those sheets. The set has no elevations, sections or roof plan, so every height and the roof are assumptions, listed below.

roof: The site plan draws the roof outline: an east-west gable over the two-story block and a north-south gable over the ground floor wing that ends in a Dutch gable, a hip below a small gable, at the street. No pitch or height is printed; at an assumed 5:12 pitch the two roofs meet where the site plan shows.
header: Window and door widths are traced from the floor plans. The set has no elevations, so window and door heights are assumed. The two entries to unit 1 follow the owner's sketch, one on each side of the ground floor.
partition: Room names and sizes are shown as printed on the plans. Each of the two inside stairs is drawn with six treads, so each climbs half a level: from the basement up to the ground floor, and from the ground floor up to the first floor. At an assumed 7 1/2 inch riser the ground floor sits 4'-4 1/2" above the basement and the first floor 8'-9". The first floor kitchen, dining area and living room are one open space; the lines between them follow the printed room sizes.

assumptions: Walls are read from the architect's vector floor plans at 3/16 inch = 1 foot and checked against the printed dimension strings: the two-story block is 30'-0" by 24'-11" and the ground floor wing 23'-0" by about 19'-4".

No heights are printed. Each inside stair is drawn with six treads (seven risers); at 7 1/2 inch risers the ground floor sits 4'-4 1/2" and the first floor 8'-9" above the basement floor. Ceilings on the ground and first floors are assumed 8'-0".
Windows are traced from the plans; their heights are assumed: sills 3'-0" and heads 6'-10" above each floor, with basement sills 4'-0" above the floor to clear the ground.

The ground is assumed level, 3'-0" above the basement floor and 1'-4 1/2" below the ground floor, from the outside stair drawn on the north side. The site plan contours fall a few feet toward the street; that slope is not modeled.
The roof follows the outline on the site plan with 18 inch overhangs. The pitch is assumed 5:12, which brings the two ridges to meet within a foot of where the site plan draws it.

The two basement options on the sheets are crossed out, so the basement is shown as it stands, including the walls the demolition plan marks in red. The ground floor and first floor follow the owner's conversion sketch: an entry to unit 1 on each side of the ground floor and the stair between the ground and first floors opened up.
A few printed room areas do not match their printed sizes (the breakfast nook, the master bedroom and the basement bedrooms); room labels show the sheet's values as printed.

The outside stair to the first floor door is drawn on the plans; the stair down to the basement door beside it is cut off at the sheet edge, so its well and steps are assumed. An angled stair shown with a break line under the first floor at the east landing is not modeled because the sheets do not show where it goes.
Interior doors are shown as open gaps. Kitchen and bath fixtures, closet shelving, siding and trim are not modeled.
